svg.text: #594 Enterprise GPU Cold-Start Acceleration: 510s → 17.5s (29.1x Faster) via Model Streamer & P2P
Cloud & AI Solution Architect Guide · Nydus/Dragonfly Lazy Image (3.5s) + Run:ai/Tensorizer O_DIRECT to HBM (11.2s) + Warm Inductor Cache (2.8s)
1. Anatomy of a 70B-FP8 (70GB) K8s Pod Scale-Up
✕ Default K8s Cold Start: 510 Seconds (8.5 Minutes!)
• 1. Docker Pull 22GB CUDA/vLLM image across 10 nodes: 180s (Registry bottleneck)
• 2. HF Hub HTTP download 70GB safetensors to disk + page-cache copy: 285s
• 3. Cold CUDA Graph / TorchInductor JIT compile: 45s → Total = 510.0s
✓ 3-Stage Accelerated Cold Start: 17.5 Seconds (29.1x Speedup!)
• Stage 1 (3.5s): Nydus / AWS SOCI Lazy Image + Dragonfly P2P (No full 22GB pull)
• Stage 2 (11.2s): Run:ai Model Streamer / Tensorizer (32-thread O_DIRECT / GDS
streams pre-sharded TP weights at 6.25 GB/s directly to Pinned DRAM / GPU HBM)
• Stage 3 (2.8s): Pre-warmed Shared Read-Only TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR
• New 70B Replica Serves First Request in 17.5s During 09:00 AM Traffic Surge!
2. How Cold-Start Latency Dictates Idle GPU Buffer Cost
The Over-Provisioning Buffer Formula: B_warm = ΔQPS_ramp × T_cold_start
• At T_cold = 510s (8.5 min), traffic can surge +55% before a new pod boots
• Forces SREs to keep +60% permanent idle GPU buffer (32 GPUs → 52 GPUs paid 24/7!)
With 17.5s Fast Boot + KEDA Pre-Prefill Queue-Depth Trigger
• Scale-up triggers on vllm:num_requests_waiting > 4 (NOT lagging CPU/GPU util%!)
• Required warm idle buffer drops from +60% (20 extra GPUs) to +10% (4 extra GPUs)
Host DRAM Checkpoint-Restore (CRIU / cuda-checkpoint: 2.4 Seconds)
• For warm nodes: NVIDIA driver cuda-checkpoint swaps VRAM state in 2.4s!
3. Financial Savings on a 32-H100 Base Fleet
• 510s Slow Boot Fleet (32 Base + 20 Buffer = 52× H100): $119,600/month.
• 17.5s Fast Boot Fleet (32 Base + 4 Buffer = 36× H100): $82,800/month (Saves 16× H100 = $36,800/mo / -30.8%!).
